maria_support: Heads up — Banyan reporting a burst this morning causing 5xxs + high tail latency on their Dedicated pool. They say admission control started rejecting requests around 06:02 PST. Escalating @ryan_sre @anya_eng
ryan_sre: Got it. Which pool and model? Any request IDs or sample logs?
maria_support: pool_id=ded-banyan-3, model=text-xxl-v1, customer timezone PST. Sample log from their app (sanitized):
```
2026-03-16T06:02:18Z admission_controller: DENY reason=burst_credits_exhausted tokens/sec=127 tokens_per_second_limit=100 headroom_tokens=10 credits_remaining=0
2026-03-16T06:02:19Z serving: 503 client=api key=banyan-xxx request_id=abc123
```
ops-bot: alert: dedicated-pool-high-rejects ded-banyan-3 06:02 -> autoscaler attempted add_nodes=2 but nodes_ready=0 after 90s
anya_eng: That log pretty clearly shows burst credits exhausted. Two parallel things: (1) refill rate too low for this customer's burst shape, (2) headroom / admission thresholds are preventing graceful degradation. Any config change recently on that pool?
maria_support: Customer says no config change on their side. They ran a scheduled data ingestion at 06:00 that spiked requests ~2x baseline for ~4 minutes. They provided a request sample for repro: `req=abc123` and this redacted header: `Authorization: Bearer banyan-***`
ryan_sre: Can we reproduce locally against ded-banyan-3? Anya, what load pattern would cause this?
anya_eng: Repro steps I recommend (low-friction):
1) Grab a small worker machine and run the load script with the customer headers.
2) Target 200 rps, payload ~300 tokens/request for 60s.
Example: `python tools/loadgen.py --host https://api.redwood.example --pool ded-banyan-3 --rps 200 --duration 60 --tokens 300 --apikey banyan-REDACT`
Or quick wrk: `wrk -t12 -c120 -d60s --latency http://ded-banyan-3.streaming/stream.lua`
that should reproduce the admission_denied log above.
maria_support: Banyan infra says they can throttle the job if needed. They're standing by.
banyan_infra: We can add exponential backoff on our crawler, will try a 30s ramp-down now. Thanks for the repro hints.
ryan_sre: Short-term mitigation plan: (A) temporarily increase admission_control.headroom from 10 tokens to 25 for ded-banyan-3; (B) bump burst_refill_rate by 2x for 2 hours; (C) enable fallback route to `text-xxl-v1-quant` for non-SLA-critical endpoints. Any objections?
anya_eng: +1 on those. We'll also add a short-term telemetry flag to surfacing `credits_remaining` per-customer in the Console so support can react faster. I can push the config change as an emergency rollout in ~20m.
maria_support: Customer asked for ETA. Can you confirm time to change and whether a restart or reload is required?
anya_eng: No restart expected; admission config supports hot reload. ETA ~20m to push and validate. I'll post logs after the change.
ryan_sre: Operational checklist (I'll own):
- [ ] push headroom + refill change (anya)
- [ ] validate deny rate drops in 10/30/60s windows (maria)
- [ ] ask Banyan to throttle job for 10m during change (maria)
- [ ] follow-up postmortem if this repeats (ryan)
I'll open an incident ticket: https://redwood/incidents/INC-2026-314 (placeholder)
maria_support: Banyan confirms they're throttling the crawler by 40% for the next 15m. :thumbsup:
banyan_infra: Confirmed — throttling in place, will report if we still see 5xxs after your change.
anya_eng: Pushed temp config to ded-banyan-3: headroom_tokens=25, burst_refill_multiplier=2. Monitoring now.
ops-bot: metric update: reject_rate ded-banyan-3 dropped from 18% -> 2% within 45s of config change
maria_support: Can confirm customer reports immediate drop in 503s. They see higher latency on a few in-flight requests but overall success rates improved.
ryan_sre: Great. Next steps:
- Make headroom change a template for customers with heavy scheduled bursts (runbook update)
- Add a guard in Console: recommend `planned_burst` alert that auto-suggests headroom bump
- Add a billing/auth correlation check to support playbook: sometimes token accounting glitches appear concurrent with auth retries (we saw a few repeated auth attempts in logs)
maria_support: I'll schedule a short call to review longer-term headroom planning and update Banyan on recommended autoscale and burst credits sizing.
banyan_infra: Thanks team. We'll try to smooth our ingestion schedule and follow your recommendations. Appreciate the fast response.
ryan_sre: Closing thread for now; we'll keep the incident open for follow-up. If anyone sees a repeat spike, re-open here.
